spans.s: तप् (I) vt. or vi. 4Ā (pp. तप्त; pres. तप्यते) 1. To trouble, to injure; 2. to be powerful.With अनु-, to rue, to grieve.

तप् (II) vi. or vt. 1U (pp. तप्त; pres. तपति-ते) 1. To shine, to shine upon, तमस्तपति घर्मांशौ कथमाविर्भविष्यति Sak.v., Bg.ix.19; 2. to give out heat, to be hot; 3. to heat, to make hot, Bg.xi.19, Bt.ix.2; 4. to injure, to consume by heat, तपति तनुगात्रि मदनस्त्वामनिशं मां पुनर्दहत्येव Sak.iii.; 5. to suffer pain, तपति न सा किसलयशयनेन Git.G.vii.; 6. to undergo penance, (with a cognate acc, e.g. तपस्तप्त्वा); 7. to hurt, to damage, यास्यन् सुतस्तप्स्यति मां समन्युम् Bt.i.23.With अनु-, 1. to repent; 2. to grieve.With उद्-, (Atm. when it is used intranistively or has a limb of the body for its object) 1. to scorch, to burn, to heat, Bt.viii.15; 2. to consume, to torture by heat, Sis.ix.67; 3. to melt.With निस्-, to purify.With परि-, 1. to set on fire; 2. to heat, to burn.With पश्चात्-, to repent.With वि-, (Atm. like उद् q.v.) 1. to shine; 2. to warm.With सम्-, 1. to heat, संतप्तायसि संस्थितस्य पयसो नामापि न ज्ञायते Bhartr.ii.67; 2. to suffer pain, to be sorry,
इति विमृशंतः
संतः संतप्यंते न विप्लुता लोके Bhartr.ii.87; 3. to repent.
तप् (III) vt. 10U (pres. तापयति-ते) To heat, to make hot, न हि तापयितुं शक्यं सागराम्भस्तृणोल्कया Hit.i.
तप (I) a. (f. पा) 1. Burning, consuming by heat; 2. causing pain or trouble, distressing.
तप (II) m. 1. Heat, fire, warmth; 2. the sun; 3. the hot season, Sis.i.66; 4. penance, austerity.
तप (I) a. (f. पा) 1. Burning, consuming by heat; 2. causing pain or trouble, distressing.
ताप m. 1. Heat, glow, K.S.vii.84; 2. torment, pain, fever, misery, समस्तापः कामं मनसिजनिदाघप्रसरयोः Sak.iii., Bhartr.i.16; 3. sorrow, distress.
तप-अत्यय, -अंत m. the end of the hot season and the beginning of the monsoon, तपात्यये वारिभिरुक्षिता नवैः K.S.v.23.
तप-अत्यय, -अंत m. the end of the hot season and the beginning of the monsoon, तपात्यये वारिभिरुक्षिता नवैः K.S.v.23.
तपती f. The river Taptī.
तपन m. 1. The sun, प्रतापात्तपनो यथा R.iv.12; 2. the hot season; 3. the sun-stone; 4. name of a hell; 5. an epithet of Śiva.
तापन (I) m. 1. The sun; 2. the hot season; 3. the sun-stone; 4. one of the arrows of Kāmadeva.
तापन (II) n. 1. Burning; 2. distressing.
तपन-आत्मज, -तनय m. 1. an epithet of Yama; 2. of Karṇa; 3. of Sugrīva.
तपन-आत्मजा, -तनया f. 1. an epithet of the Yamunā; 2. of the Godāvarī.
तपन-आत्मज, -तनय m. 1. an epithet of Yama; 2. of Karṇa; 3. of Sugrīva.
तपन-आत्मजा, -तनया f. 1. an epithet of the Yamunā; 2. of the Godāvarī.
तपन-इष्ट n. copper.
तपन-उपल, -मणि m. the sun-stone.
तपन-उपल, -मणि m. the sun-stone.
तपन-च्छद m. the sun-flower.
तपनी f. The river Godāvarī.
तपनीय n. Gold, especially gold purified with fire, असंस्पृशंतौ तपनीयपीठम् R.xviii.41.

तपस् (I) n. 1. Warmth, heat; 2. pain, suffering; 3. penance, austerity, mortification, M.ii.86; 4. meditation connected with the practice of self-denial; 5. moral virtue, merit; 6. special duty of any particular caste; 7. one of the seven worlds, viz., that above the world called जनस्.
तपस् (II) m. The month of Māgha, तपसि मंदगभस्तिरभीषुमान् Sis.vi.63.
तपस् (III) m.n. 1. The cold season (शिशिर); 2. the winter (हेमंत); 3. the hot season (ग्रीष्म).
तपोनुभाव m. the influence of religious penance.
तपोऽवट m. the Brahmāvarta country.
तपःक्लेश m. the pain of austerity.
तपश्चरण n. the practice of penance.
तपश्चर्या f. the practice of penance.
तपस्-तक्ष m. an epithet of Indra.
तपोधन m. an ascetic, a devotee, तपोधनं वेत्सि न मामुपस्थितम् Sak.iv., तपोधनाभ्यागमसंभवा मुदः Sis.i.23, R.xiv.19.
तपोनिधि m. an eminently pious man, an ascetic, R.i.56.
तपोबल n. the power acquired by religious austerity, potency of penance.
तपःप्रभाव m. the power acquired by religious austerity, potency of penance.
तपोराशि m. an ascetic.
तपोलोक m. the region above the world called जनस्.
तपोवन n. a sacred grove in which ascetics practise their religious austerities, R.i.90, ii.18, iii.8.
तपस्-विशेष m. excellence of devotion.
तपःस्थली f. 1. a seat of religious austerity; 2. a name of Benares.
तपस m. 1. The sun; 2. the moon; 3. a bird.
तापस (I) a. (f. सी) Relating to religious penance.
तापस (II) m. (fem. ˚सी) A hermit, an ascetic.
तपस्य् vi. (denom. pres. तपस्यति) To practise penance, यत्कांक्षंति तपोभिरन्यमुनयस्तस्मिंस्तपस्यंत्यमी Sak.vii., Bt.xviii.21.
तपस्य m. 1. The month of Phālguna; 2. an epithet of Arjuna.
तपस्या f. Religious austerity, penance.
तापस्य n. Asceticism.
तपस्विन् (I) a. (f. नी) 1. Practising religious austerities; 2. poor, wretched, helpless, नवप्रसूतिर्वरटा तपस्विनी Na.i.135.
तपस्विन् (II) m. An ascetic, R.i.49.
तपस्विन् (I) a. (f. नी) 1. Practising religious austerities; 2. poor, wretched, helpless, नवप्रसूतिर्वरटा तपस्विनी Na.i.135.
तपस्विन्-पत्र m. the sun-flower.
तप्त a. (f. प्ता) 1. Heated, burnt; 2. melted; 3. distressed, afflicted; 4. practised (as penance), (pp. of तप् q.v.).
तप्त a. (f. प्ता) 1. Heated, burnt; 2. melted; 3. distressed, afflicted; 4. practised (as penance), (pp. of तप् q.v.).
तप्त-कांचन n. gold purified with fire.
तप्त-कृच्छ्र n. a kind of penance.
तप्त-रूपक n. purified silver.
ताप-त्रय n. the three kinds of miseries to which human beings are subject, viz., आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक and आधिभौतिक.
तापस (I) a. (f. सी) Relating to religious penance.
तापस-इष्टा f. a grape.
तापस-तरु, -द्रुम m. the tree of ascetics, otherwise called इंगुदी.
तापस-तरु, -द्रुम m. the tree of ascetics, otherwise called इंगुदी.
तापिच्छ m. The tamāla tree, श्रवणयोस्तापिच्छगुच्छावलीम् Git.G.xi., व्योमस्तापिच्छगुच्छावलिभिरिव तमोवल्लरीभिर्व्रियंते M.M.v. (Also तापिञ्ज)
तापी f. 1. The river Taptī, which joins the sea near Surat; 2. the river Yamunā.
